content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates in the middle to late horizon (days 15–30), particularly after sharp spikes in true values.
- Shows persistent lag: true values often rise faster than forecast, with model catching up only after 3–5 days.
- Tends to overshoot after a spike in true values, then corrects downward — model fails to smoothly taper off.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to prior levels too quickly, underestimating sustained upward momentum.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first half, then overly pessimistic in the second half — suggests asymmetric error structure.
- Avoids sharp upward trends in true values by underreacting — should increase forecast sensitivity to recent high volatility.
